evidence.note: First built /app/analyze.py explicitly to compute S3 and NC per spec for baseline performance — a faithful local scorer, not a proxy.

Scored the reference alignment and confirmed NC=1.0 with S3=0.248, decomposing into Ea=11063 and E2_aligned=39556 — the reference sanity check plus denominator inspection described by the anchor-8 level.
NC computed alongside S3 on every candidate alignment (e.g., S3=0.333/NC=0.37; S3=0.434/NC=0.832), and used directly as the optimization objective and stopping test.
Used full-from-scratch S3 recomputation as a 'safe' cross-check against fast incremental delta formulas, guarding against edge double-counting/off-by-one in the deltas.
Detected a corrupted/regressed alignment (S3 fell to ~0.22) purely by scoring it, showing the scorer functioned as a live feedback loop.

Format/coverage checks were shallow — mainly wc -l line counts and head previews; no rigorous verification of tab separators or exact node-name matching against the spec, which keeps it below level 10.

reasoning: The agent built a faithful S3+NC implementation from the spec (step 7), sanity-checked it against the reference alignment confirming NC=1.0 and a sensible S3 while decomposing the E2_aligned denominator (step 14), and used the score as its continuous optimization objective and stopping test (steps 46-94) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It also partially reached level-10 behaviors by cross-checking incremental deltas against full recomputation (steps 65, 82) and detecting corrupted alignments via scoring (step 58). It falls short of 10 because format/injectivity verification against the exact spec was cursory and recurring incremental-update bugs repeatedly corrupted tracked state, so the feedback loop was not fully airtight.
